note: Papers are those where an Aurora member is the first or second author, PLUS papers from Aurora-led JWST surveys (VENUS, led by S. Fujimoto; MINERVA, led by A. Muzzin), which are included regardless of author position and attributed to the survey lead. Recent items prioritize member-first-author papers. Authorship checked against the arXiv author list; 'venue' set only for papers confirmed published; dates follow the arXiv posting, or the journal publication when that is the news event. Links point to the ADS record. Do not add unverified papers, awards, figures, or venues.

items.title: SN Helios: a multiply imaged Type II supernova opening time-delay cosmography beyond redshift of 3
items.blurb: JWST imaging from the VENUS survey and a NIRSpec prism spectrum identify SN Helios as a multiply imaged Type II supernova at z = 3.34, with another image predicted within about 2–6 years for a time-delay measurement of H₀.

items.title: A tidal disruption event in a quasar at redshift 7.19
items.blurb: More than two decades of HST, Spitzer, and JWST imaging reveal a long-lived nuclear transient in the red quasar GNz7q at z = 7.19 that points to the tidal disruption of a star of a few solar masses.

items.title: A dense, metal-rich absorber driven by a heavily dust-obscured galaxy: the direct evidence of CGM enrichment at z ∼ 7
items.blurb: JWST and NOEMA link a dense, metal-enriched absorber at z = 7.03 to ND1, a heavily dust-obscured starburst about 16 kpc from the quasar sightline whose 64 M⊙ yr⁻¹ outflow appears to carry metals into its halo.

items.title: Early steps in the hierarchical assembly of a Milky Way-mass galaxy 1 Gyr after the Big Bang
items.blurb: JWST spectra of three interacting, lensed low-mass galaxies at z = 5.196, expected to grow into a Milky Way-mass galaxy, suggest intense star-forming bursts boost their stellar mass growth to 2.6 ± 0.5 times that of merging alone.

items.title: A sub-100 pc view at z ∼ 5 of a multiply-imaged massive quiescent galaxy
items.blurb: VENUS NIRCam imaging of the lensed post-starburst galaxy VENUS-CLJ0152-QG1 at z ≈ 5.2 reaches about 70 pc resolution and reveals a size twice that expected and a low central density, pointing to quenching without compaction.

items.title: A systematic assessment of total stellar mass measurements with spatially resolved photometry and medium bands at 1 < z < 9
items.blurb: Resolved JWST and HST photometry of about 3000 galaxies at 1 < z < 9 shows that integrated photometry underestimates stellar masses, by a median of about 0.36 dex in galaxies with high specific star formation rates, consistent with outshining.

items.title: Distance estimation using globular clusters and ultra-compact dwarfs
items.blurb: A bilinear relation between absolute magnitude and dynamical mass for globular clusters and ultra-compact dwarfs gives per-object distance uncertainties of about 30–35% and places the debated dwarf galaxy NGC1052-DF2 at 19.1 ± 4.3 Mpc.

items.title: Model predictive scoring shows specific BAO observations (not SNIa) drives w₀wₐ tension
items.blurb: Scoring ΛCDM and w₀wₐCDM by how well each predicts held-out data traces the modest preference for evolving dark energy to a single DESI BAO measurement at z = 0.706, while the supernova datasets show no preference.

items.title: The second Little UV Camera (LUVCam2) mission
items.blurb: LUVCam2, an 80 mm dual ultraviolet-optical telescope designed to observe UV flares from low-mass stars, is planned to fly on the CubeSat BRNOsat in late 2027 with a backside-illuminated CMOS sensor for higher UV quantum efficiency.

items.title: A report on the first technology demonstration mission of the Little UV Camera (LUVCam1)
items.blurb: LUVCam1, a 0.4U payload on the 2U cubesat GRBBeta launched in July 2024, tests the GSENSE4040 CMOS sensor in orbit ahead of the QUVIK ultraviolet mission and remains operational two years later.

items.title: Automated multi-stressor optical fiber focal ratio degradation and throughput characterization system
items.blurb: An automated test bench measures focal ratio degradation and throughput of optical fibers under varied input angle, wavelength, bending, twist, and load, built for future survey facilities such as Spec-S5 and WST with more than 25,000 fibers.

items.title: Hidden mass in early galaxies revealed by bottom-heavy initial mass functions
items.blurb: Ultra-deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra of nine massive quiescent galaxies at z ≈ 0.7 reveal bottom-heavy stellar initial mass functions, an excess of low-mass stars that raises their inferred stellar masses.

items.title: The low-mass baryon cycle in QUEST dwarf galaxies I: sample definition and first results
items.blurb: The first-release QUEST Dwarfs sample of 14 galaxies indicates that chemically enriched cool gas is concentrated in the inner circumgalactic medium, where it holds ≈3% and ≈16% of the metals produced by lower- and higher-mass dwarfs.

items.title: The road to normalcy: environment-driven evolutionary pathways for primordial black holes
items.blurb: Hydrodynamical simulations show that primordial black hole seeds follow environment-dependent pathways, forming faint, metal-poor systems in underdense regions and growing rapidly in overdense ones, with compact sources resembling Little Red Dots appearing as one evolutionary phase.

items.title: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
items.blurb: Hα imaging with the partially completed MOTHRA telescope finds twenty-two compact bow shocks around gas clumps in the outer Helix Nebula, which the team interprets as AGB-shell fragments stripped by the interstellar medium and losing coherence within about 10,000 years.

items.title: EncoTESS: age-sensitive encodings from raw TESS light curves
items.blurb: EncoTESS, a compact time-series foundation model trained on TESS 2-minute light curves, turns raw stellar variability into encodings that track age better than rotation period or variability amplitude for young K and M stars.

items.title: VENUS: an ultra-faint galaxy hosting the metal-poor Type II supernova at z = 5.13
items.blurb: The first characterization of the host of the multiply imaged Type IIP supernova SN Eos at z = 5.13, where a total magnification of about 53 lets the team resolve the supernova's local environment inside an ultra-faint early galaxy.

items.title: Boötes III is a tidally disrupting ultra-faint dwarf galaxy on an eccentric polar orbit
items.blurb: Twenty-one member stars show that Boötes III is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy being tidally disrupted on a highly eccentric polar orbit, caught about 0.14 Gyr after its latest pericentric passage.

items.title: Clues to inside-out quenching in quiescent galaxies at 1.2 ≲ z ≲ 2.2: age, Fe-, and Mg-abundance gradients from JWST-SUSPENSE
items.blurb: Spatially resolved ages and abundances in eight massive quiescent galaxies at 1.2 ≲ z ≲ 2.2 show cores that are older, and possibly Mg-poor, compared to their outskirts, supporting inside-out quenching.

items.title: Light, heavy, primordial: exploring the diversity of black hole seeding and growth mechanisms in the JWST era
items.blurb: A unified comparison of light, heavy, and primordial black hole seeding and growth channels against the JWST census of early massive black holes, including the over-massive systems found in metal-poor hosts.

items.title: The THESAN-ZOOM project: Mystery N/O more – uncovering the origin of peculiar chemical abundances and a not-so-fundamental metallicity relation at 3 < z < 12
items.blurb: THESAN-ZOOM simulations show smoothly curved mass-metallicity relations already in place at z ≈ 12, governed by how well galaxies retain their metals, while the fundamental metallicity relation inverts for gas in low-mass galaxies.

items.title: First statistical study of over 100 magnified stellar events at redshift z ≈ 0.725 with JWST
items.blurb: More than 100 magnified stellar events in the lensed Dragon galaxy at z ≈ 0.725, found in three cycles of JWST imaging behind Abell 370, constrain the bright end of the stellar luminosity function and trace the cluster's critical curves.

items.title: The kinematically hot, extremely metal-poor C-19 stellar stream in DESI DR2
items.blurb: Using DESI DR2 radial velocities and metallicities to characterize the C-19 stream, whose large velocity dispersion is hard to explain with a purely baryonic, disrupting globular-cluster progenitor.

items.title: The in situ growth of stellar-mass "light" seed black holes in nuclear star clusters
items.blurb: Magnetohydrodynamic simulations of how stellar-mass "light" seed black holes, the remnants of massive stars, form and grow inside nuclear star clusters as a possible channel toward supermassive black holes.

items.title: VENUS: strong-lensing model of MACS J1931.8-2635 – revealing the farthest multiply imaged supernova
items.blurb: A strong-lensing model of the cluster MACS J1931.8-2635 from the JWST VENUS survey, accompanying the spectroscopically confirmed supernova SN Eos at z = 5.13 and revealing new multiply imaged systems.

items.title: Hedorah, the first yellow supergiant Kaiju star candidate at z = 3.7 revealed by JWST behind AS1063
items.blurb: A new free-form lens model of the cluster AS1063, built from spectroscopically confirmed lensed galaxies and ultra-deep GLIMPSE imaging, also turns up Hedorah, a lensed yellow-supergiant star candidate at z ≈ 3.7.

items.title: VENUS: when red meets blue – a multiply imaged Little Red Dot with an apparent blue companion behind the galaxy cluster Abell 383
items.blurb: A doubly-imaged Little Red Dot candidate (A383-LRD1) behind the cluster Abell 383, with an apparent compact blue companion, from the JWST VENUS survey.

items.title: Black hole merger rates in the first billion years in light of JWST data
items.blurb: Modeling black-hole merger rates in the first billion years to test light- versus heavy-seed scenarios against the abundance of faint AGN that JWST finds at z = 4–9.

items.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: JWST/IFU optical observations for 18 main-sequence galaxies at z = 4–6
items.blurb: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey combines kpc-resolved HST, JWST, and ALMA imaging and spectroscopy of 18 main-sequence galaxies at z = 4–6 to resolve their stars, gas, and dust together.

items.title: The superclustering of hot gas: cosmological sensitivity in the WebSky simulations
items.blurb: Orientation-aware summary statistics of the superclustering of hot gas in the WebSky simulations, sharpening the cosmological sensitivity of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich and galaxy cross-correlations.

items.title: The WebSky [CII] forecasts and the search for primordial intermittent non-Gaussianity
items.blurb: WebSky [CII] line-intensity mock maps that forecast upcoming wide-field submillimeter surveys (matched to CCAT) of cosmological [CII] emission from the epoch of reionization.

items.title: MINERVA: a NIRCam medium-band and MIRI imaging survey to unlock the hidden gems of the distant Universe
items.blurb: An overview of MINERVA, a JWST Cycle 4 treasury program of 8-band NIRCam medium-band and MIRI imaging across four CANDELS fields, designed to uncover distant and dust-obscured galaxies.

items.title: Quantitative morphology of Galactic cirrus in deep optical imaging
items.blurb: A morphological study of optical Galactic cirrus in deep imaging, using intensity statistics, angular power spectra, and wavelets to characterize the diffuse interstellar medium.

items.title: Synergising semi-analytical models and hydrodynamical simulations to interpret JWST data from the first billion years
items.blurb: Feeding cold-gas fractions and star-formation efficiencies from the SPHINX20 radiation-hydrodynamics simulation into the DELPHI semi-analytic model to explain the abundance of bright galaxies at z ≥ 11 and the drivers of reionization.

items.title: GLIMPSE: an ultra-faint Pop III galaxy candidate and first constraints on the Pop III UV luminosity function at z ≈ 6–7
items.blurb: A NIRCam-based search across ~500 arcmin² of JWST legacy fields turns up GLIMPSE-16043, a promising ultra-faint Population III galaxy candidate at z ≈ 6.5, and sets first limits on the Pop III UV luminosity function.
